notes:
Summary: EchoRidge is a mid-market support automation vendor building a hosted+managed offering for SMB and mid-market customers. They ingest multi-channel tickets (email, web, chat) and want to add automatic short summaries for agent handoff + auto-tagging to drive routing and macros in Zendesk/Freshdesk. Key asks: reliable P95 latency under spikes, deterministic tagging schema mapping to existing triggers, write-back to ticket fields, and audit logs for compliance.

Requirements / constraints (from calls):
- Workloads: ~4k incoming tickets/day currently; expected 3x seasonal spikes (Black Friday style) — peak ingestion expected ~500 tickets/min for short windows (10-30 minutes).
- Targets: summary generation P95 <= 1.5s under normal load; P95 <= 3s during spikes; tagging accuracy >= 92% for top-10 tags; rollbacks for wrong tags via webhook macro.
- Cost sensitivity: high for per-ticket processing; prefer quantized/13B-class models for steady-state, larger models for fallbacks on low-volume high-value accounts.
- Integrations: Zendesk + Freshdesk primary. Need pre-built app or webhook templates that can: 1) post summary -> private note, 2) update tags/fields, 3) trigger macro on confidence thresholds.
- Security: SSO/SAML, audit logs for all write-backs, KMS integration for key management, EU data residency for a subset of tenants.
- Model preferences: open-model first approach (Llama-2/3 13B quantized) for cost; allow fallback route to larger hosted model for complex threads. Also interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching/caching and KV cache reuse for multi-message threads.
- Reliability & fallbacks: must support routing policy to degrade to async batch enrichment if realtime capacity constrained; prefer graceful degradation to second-tier model or enqueue for agent review with reason codes.

POC plan (EchoRidge proposed):
- Phase 0 (1 week): integration checklist + security kickoff (get SSO and SOC2 Qs).
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): sandbox with sample ticket stream (Zendesk dev org) — implement summarization + tag inference, test write-back. Goal: 500 tickets/day equivalent for functional validation.
- Phase 2 (4 weeks pilot): run against production-sampled traffic with A/B (no-write vs. write) for tag accuracy and latency metrics; measure impact on agent handle time.
- Success criteria: P95 latency goals met, tag precision/recall above 90%, write-back reliability >= 99.9% for accepted tags, and no security blockers.

Key quotes / snippets from stakeholders:
- "We need something that doesn't slow down agents or create more noise — tags must be useful, not decorative." — Head of Support Product
- "If you can show consistent behavior during peak minutes, we'll fast-track procurement." — CTO

Open items / blockers:
- Confirm EU data residency approach for multi-tenant customers (controlled by routing policy).
- Legal wants example DPA + encryption-in-transit / at-rest language. SE to provide template.
- Need Zendesk app permissions: currently sandbox has read-only; require admin enable for ticket write-back.

Suggested Redwood playbook items for SE / AE:
- Prepare a pilot SOW with explicit spike SLOs and rollback triggers for tags.
- Build a quick mapping guide: predicted_tag -> Zendesk_field/macro. Ship as part of pilot repo.
- Run small stress test (simulated 600 t/min for 20 minutes) in dedicated test cluster to demonstrate graceful degradation and fallback routing.

Final notes: EchoRidge feels time-sensitive (Q4 procurement cycle). They are pragmatic — will accept hybrid (hosted for bulk, dedicated pools for peaks) if pricing is clear. Good chance to land a multi-month pilot that expands to dedicated contract if spike guarantees and security answers are satisfactory.
